Randolph's Free-Marginal Multirater Kappa

Source: R/randolphKappa.R
randolphKappa.Rd

Computes Randolph's free-marginal multirater kappa for \(m\) raters over \(N\) subjects. This agreement coefficient does not assume fixed marginal distributions (i.e., it is free-marginal).

randolphKappa(x, conf.level = NA, ...)

Arguments

x

a matrix of size \(N \times m\) with subjects in rows and raters in columns; cells contain the assigned categories

conf.level

reserved for future confidence intervals and currently ignored

...

reserved for future bootstrap options and currently ignored

Value

a numeric scalar containing Randolph's kappa

Details

Let \(k\) be the number of distinct categories across all ratings, \(m\) the number of raters, and \(N\) the number of subjects. Randolph's kappa is $$\kappa = \frac{P_o - 1/k}{1 - 1/k},$$ where the observed agreement \(P_o\) is $$P_o = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \frac{\max_j n_{ij}}{m}.$$ Here, \(n_{ij}\) denotes the number of raters who assigned subject \(i\) to category \(j\); \(\max_j n_{ij}\) is the modal (most frequent) category count per subject.

Long-format ratings can first be reshaped with raterFrame.

References

Randolph, J. J. (2005). Free-Marginal Multirater Kappa (multirater \(\kappa_{\mathrm{free}}\)): An Alternative to Fleiss’ Fixed-Marginal Multirater Kappa. Online submission.

See also

Other assoc.agreement: blandAltmanData(), ccc(), cohenKappa(), cronbachAlpha(), icc(), kappaM(), krippAlpha(), normalizeToConfusion(), pabak(), percAgreement(), raterFrame()

Examples

## Matrix (subjects x raters), 5 subjects, 3 raters
x <- matrix(c(
  1,1,1,
  2,2,2,
  1,2,1,
  3,3,3,
  2,2,1
), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
randolphKappa(x)
#> [1] 0.8

## Long format with a formula
df <- data.frame(
  subject = rep(1:5, each = 3),
  rater   = rep(paste0("r", 1:3), times = 5),
  rating  = c(1,1,1, 2,2,2, 1,2,1, 3,3,3, 2,2,1)
)
randolphKappa(raterFrame(rating ~ subject | rater, 
                         data = df, dropSubj=TRUE))
#> [1] 0.8
